experiences.title: GenAI Engineer interview at a mid-size fintech
experiences.totalDuration: About 3 weeks from application to offer
experiences.summary: Four rounds covering Python and SQL screening, a deep RAG discussion, an LLM evaluation system design round and a hiring manager chat. The RAG and evaluation rounds were the hardest.

rounds.title: Online assessment
rounds.summary: Two coding questions, one SQL question and 15 ML and LLM MCQs. Cut-off was roughly two coding questions plus 70% on MCQs.

questions.text: Given a list of document chunks with embeddings, return the top-k most similar chunks to a query vector without using any vector library (cosine similarity in plain Python or NumPy).
Merge overlapping intervals. Then extend it: merge overlapping text spans that come from the same document when building a citation list.
Write a SQL query to find the top 3 users by number of LLM requests per day, along with their average latency, from a table requests(user_id, created_at, latency_ms).

solution.label: Top N per group with window functions

questions.text: MCQs: what does temperature do to the softmax over logits, which metric is best for imbalanced classification, and what is the purpose of KV caching.

rounds.title: Technical round 1: RAG deep dive
rounds.summary: Started with a walkthrough of my RAG project, then the interviewer kept pushing on failure modes: why retrieval was bad, how I knew, and what I changed.

questions.text: Walk me through your RAG pipeline end to end. Why did you pick that chunk size and overlap, and how did you validate the choice?
Dense retrieval returns plausible but wrong chunks for queries with exact product codes. How do you fix it?

solution.label: Hybrid search: BM25 plus dense retrieval

questions.text: What is the difference between a bi-encoder and a cross-encoder? Where does a reranker sit and what latency does it add?
How would you reduce hallucinations when the retrieved context does not contain the answer?

rounds.title: Technical round 2: LLM evaluation system design
rounds.mode: Video call with a shared whiteboard
rounds.summary: One open-ended design question with several follow-ups on metrics, cost and online monitoring.

questions.text: Design an evaluation pipeline for a customer-support RAG assistant. What do you measure offline, and what do you monitor in production?
How would you use an LLM as a judge, and how do you check that the judge itself is reliable (position bias, verbosity bias, agreement with humans)?
Faithfulness, answer relevance and context precision: define each and say which one you would alert on first.
Your eval set has 200 questions and a prompt change improves the score by 2 points. How do you decide if it is real?

rounds.title: Hiring manager and HR
rounds.summary: Mostly project ownership and behavioural questions, then a short discussion on notice period and expectations.

questions.text: Tell me about a time a model or pipeline you built failed in production or in a demo. What did you do?
Why GenAI engineering and not classical ML? Where do you want to be in two years?

tips: Know your own project to the last detail: chunk size, embedding model, top-k, latency and what you measured.
Have a concrete failure story for retrieval and be ready to explain how you diagnosed it.
For the design round, start with metrics and data before drawing boxes.

experiences.title: AI Engineer intern interview at an early-stage AI startup
experiences.summary: A take-home RAG assignment, a live review of that assignment with agent-focused follow-ups, and a short founder conversation. Practical and project driven, with very little data-structures content.

rounds.title: Take-home assignment
rounds.summary: Build a small question-answering service over a set of PDFs with a README explaining the trade-offs. Evaluated on the design choices as much as on the output.

questions.text: Build an API that ingests PDFs, chunks and embeds them, and answers questions with citations to the source page.

solution.label: Build a RAG pipeline with citations

questions.text: Add a small evaluation script with at least 10 question and answer pairs and report a metric of your choice.

rounds.title: Assignment review and technical discussion
rounds.summary: Screen-shared walkthrough of my submission, then follow-up questions on extending it into an agent that can call tools.

questions.text: Why did you choose this embedding model and vector store? What would you change if the corpus grew to 10 million chunks?
Turn this into an agent that can also query a SQL database. How do you decide when to retrieve and when to call the tool?
How do you stop an agent from looping forever or calling the same tool repeatedly? What do you log to debug it?
Explain structured output and function calling. How do you handle a model returning invalid JSON?

rounds.title: Founder conversation
rounds.summary: Informal chat about projects, learning speed and availability. No technical questions.

questions.text: Which of your projects are you proudest of and what would you do differently now?
How do you keep up with new LLM tools and papers, and how do you decide what is worth adopting?

tips: Write a clear README: what you built, what you skipped and why.
Even a tiny evaluation script sets a submission apart.
Be ready to extend your own code live, so keep it simple enough to modify in front of someone.
